title: Grade 7 Math — Wed, May 20
description: Probability — Day 3 of 5: Playing cards and combined events
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A standard deck has 52 cards. How many suits are there?
questions.explanation: A deck has 4 suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades — each with 13 cards.

questions.question: P(drawing a Heart from a 52-card deck) = ?
P(drawing a King from a 52-card deck) = ?
questions.explanation: There are 4 Kings (one per suit). P(King) = 4/52 = 1/13.

questions.question: P(drawing a red card from a 52-card deck) = ?
questions.explanation: Red cards = Hearts + Diamonds = 26 cards. P(red) = 26/52 = 1/2.

questions.question: Rolling two dice, what is the total number of outcomes?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 outcomes. Two dice: 6 × 6 = 36 total outcomes.

questions.question: Rolling two dice: P(getting sum = 2)?
questions.explanation: Sum = 2 only when both dice show 1: (1,1). Just 1 combination. P = 1/36.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls drawn one after another (with replacement). P(both red) = ?
P(drawing a face card from a 52-card deck)? (Face cards = Jack, Queen, King)
questions.explanation: Face cards = J, Q, K in 4 suits = 12 cards. P = 12/52 = 3/13.

questions.question: P(NOT getting a face card) from a 52-card deck = ?
A coin is tossed twice. What is the total number of outcomes?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes. Two tosses: 2 × 2 = 4. Sample space: {HH, HT, TH, TT}.

questions.question: Tossing a coin twice: P(getting at least one Head)?
questions.explanation: Outcomes: {HH, HT, TH, TT}. At least one H = HH, HT, TH = 3 outcomes. P = 3/4.

questions.question: P(drawing an Ace from a 52-card deck) = ?
Rolling a die: P(getting a number divisible by 3)?
questions.explanation: Numbers divisible by 3 on a die: 3 and 6 = 2 outcomes. P = 2/6 = 1/3.
